recruit_text.adjustment:
She landed with her scissors in her apron pocket. The first thing she did on this world was cut a grunt's hair, and he tipped her a copper.

She started praying at the Crossroads because she didn't know what else to do, and the light came down on the second day.
recruit_text.forward:
A proper salon with a door that shuts and a mirror that isn't a bucket of water.

And a church, any church, where someone will sing with her.

stages.stranger: I'm Lúcia, querido, and you've got half the Barrens in your hair. I'll heal you and I'll pray for you, and I'll fix that hair while we walk. Tell me everything about yourself.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Goiânia, in the middle of Brazil. I had my own salon, pink tiles and two chairs, a radio that only got one station, and a cat called Dona Flor asleep in the window. Saturdays there was a queue down the street. I had a boyfriend, Marcelo, for four years, but he wanted São Paulo and I didn't. We split up kindly.
stages.companion: My mother phoned me every day at noon, and I'd put her on speaker so the whole salon could join in. That's why I stop for a moment at noon, every day. I haven't found her. I was cutting a customer's hair when it happened, and I landed in the Barrens with my scissors and my grandmother's candle list in my purse.
stages.friend: My grandmother, Dona Zuleide, raised me while my mother worked. Every Sunday she lit a candle for everybody on our street, by name, and I kept the list. She died when I was twenty-five and I took over the candles. What I miss most here, meu Deus, is singing in church with other people. A tauren guard says they sing to the sun at Camp Taurajo every dawn. I want to hear it. Will you take me?
stages.sworn: It wasn't my church and it wasn't my language, and it didn't matter at all. They sang to the sun and I sang with them in Portuguese, and the sun answered both of us. An old tauren woman told me to come back every dawn I can. I've got a little shelter at the Crossroads now with a real door and a real mirror, and a candle wall. Every Sunday I light one for everybody on my grandmother's list, and for the tauren they've told me about.

moments.prompt: It's noon, and she's gone quiet for a moment.

options.text: Take as long as you need.
options.reply: Thank you, querido. She'd have liked you, she likes everybody who waits.
Yes, I'm fine. It's just noon, that's all.

moments.prompt: She's asked you to take her to Camp Taurajo.

options.text: Let's go and hear them sing.
options.reply: Nossa, do you mean it? I'm going to cry the whole way there, I warn you.

options.text: They might not want an outsider.
options.reply: Then I'll earn it. I've won over worse customers than a tauren.

lines.bored_warning: Querido, we've been doing the same thing for days and I haven't met a single new person. Can we go somewhere with people in it?
lines.leaving_good: That was wonderful, and I've got so much gossip I'm not going to tell anybody. I'm off to the Crossroads now. Come and get a haircut.
lines.leaving_bored: Nothing's happening out here, and I've got a queue waiting at the Crossroads, querido.
lines.after_wipe: Meu Deus, everybody come here and let me look at you. I'm going to pray for all of you, and you're going to let me.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here and my heart can't take it. I'll stay to the end of this one, but then I need some days at home.
lines.wipe_leave: I stayed until it was done, like I said. Now I want to sit in the sun at the Crossroads for a while.
lines.zone_warning: Querido, this place is too much for us. I can pray very hard, but I'm not sure the sun can keep up with this.
lines.zone_leave: I can't pray that hard, querido. I'll be at the Crossroads, by the inn.
lines.gear_refuse: Ah, no, I'd like to keep that, querido. When we're friends, maybe.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, take it. I'll pray a bit harder to make up for it.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece, querido. I'm only mentioning it in my prayers, mostly.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, it's beautiful, thank you! Graças a Deus for you.
lines.back: I'm back, and I've brought my scissors! Who needs a trim? You do, look at you.
lines.send_word: Lúcia has sent word from the Crossroads. Her queue's done and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked out angry, and that's not me, querido. Sit down, let me fix your hair while I tell you why, and then it's your turn.
lines.neglect: There you are! I lit a candle for you every Sunday, you know. Look, it worked.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more. But I'm fixing everybody's hair tonight.
lines.on_break: Lúcia is back at the Crossroads, cutting hair by the inn. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

town_arrive.text: Look at all these people. I want to know every one of their stories.
My cat slept in the salon window all day, every day. I look for a cat in a window in every town we walk into.

boss_down.text: Graças a Deus. Now line up, everybody, one at a time.

close_call.text: Meu Deus, I prayed so hard just then. Come here, let me see.

dungeon_clear.text: Out in the sun again, thank God. I don't like it where the light can't reach.
